note: Adapted from the species description of Sands (1972); the original is in English and the genus has no soldier caste, only the alate and worker being described; measurement tables, figure numbers, type specimens and distribution records are not translated.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Together with A. murcus it is distinguished from the other species of species group II by the very long head hairs of the alate; in A. murcus the posterior margin of the head capsule is slightly more evenly rounded, the meso- and metanotum are narrower, and the first marginal tooth of the right mandible of the worker is slightly more reduced than in this species. The worker is distinguished from all species of group II except A. mitis by the reduced third apical spur of the fore tibia, but in A. mitis the fore tibia is stouter, the postclypeus more strongly inflated and the apical tooth of the mandibles longer. A. irrixosus, which also has a reduced third apical spur, is much larger, with a longer apical tooth and a very wide notch between the accessory marginal tooth of the left mandible and the molar prominence.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule and pilosity pale yellowish brown, pilosity long and conspicuous. Postclypeus moderately inflated, Pcl/W 0.26, Pcl/Ri 2.49; apical tooth of mandibles short, La/Li 0.62, Ra/Rj 0.89; accessory marginal tooth of the left mandible separated from the molar prominence in surface view by a distinct notch, compound ratio 9.97; apical and marginal teeth of the right mandible approximately in the same line, the anterior edge of the first marginal tooth slightly longer than that of the second, compound ratio 14.20. Fore tibia hardly inflated, Ti/Ty 5.21, third apical spur reduced or absent. Junction of mesenteron and proctodaeum oblique, touching the Malpighian nodule on the right; enteric valve seating lateral in the undissected abdomen, weakly bilobed, connected to the second proctodaeal pouch by a distinct neck; membranous wall of the valve with sparse spinules outside the inner cushions. About one worker in four shows a dehiscent abdomen.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule chestnut brown, very deep above the ocelli; fontanelle almost as large as the ocellus, elongate-oval, flat or slightly depressed, brown; mid-spot oval, flat, distinctly smaller than the fontanelle, chestnut brown; postclypeus brown, labrum yellowish brown; frontal mark flat, shining, semicircular, brown; antennae yellowish brown. Pronotum and mesonotum brown, metanotum yellowish brown, a transverse dark suture present but weak on meso- and metanotum; femora pale yellowish brown, tibiae yellow, tarsi pale yellow. Abdominal tergites brown, dorsal spiracles sepia brown, sternites yellowish brown with paler middle, ventral spiracles brown; cerci pale yellowish brown. Posterior margin of head capsule rather unevenly rounded, slightly undulate immediately behind the compound eye; ocelli rather small, separated from the compound eye by slightly less than their own minimum diameter; postclypeus weakly inflated, Pcl/W 0.21, Pcl/Ra 2.48–2.67, posterior margin obtusely angled rather than rounded, median suture distinct. Apical tooth of mandibles short, La/Li 0.58–0.59, Ra/Ri 0.77–0.84; accessory marginal tooth of the left mandible separated from the molar prominence in surface view by a distinct notch, compound ratio 6.74–6.81; tips of the apical and marginal teeth of the right mandible in the same line, the anterior edge of the first marginal tooth distinctly longer than that of the second. Pilosity of head capsule brown, a coarse short felt beneath very long standing hairs, the longest setae extending far beyond the outer margin of the compound eye. Constriction between meso- and metanotum slightly wide, M/W 0.31–0.32. Third apical spur of fore tibia distinct.
